text.p: The Australian December 10-year bond futures contract held 92.000 support during Friday's SYCOM session before finishing with a slim gain over the pit close.
The contract ended afterhours trade at 92.025, a fraction above an open outcry close of 92.020.

The market is building a solid support barrier at 92.000, which is keeping the equivilent cash bond yield just below 8.0 percent, although this level is likely to come under pressure in the run-up to Tuesday's FOMC meeting, traders said.
U.S. Treasuries also showed modest gains on Friday as the debate over whether the Fed will tighten continued.
A Reuters survey showed 17 out of 30 economists expect the Fed to tighten at the meeting, while out of the remaining 13, seven expect a hike in November.

The local market finally showed some caution to the possibility of a U.S. tightening on Friday, after steadily outperforming U.S. bonds for most of last week, and breached a two-week upward trendline at around 92.040.
A move above 92.070 would re-establish this trendline, although there is stiff resistance at 92.060, traders added.
No local economic figures are due for release on Monday.
